issue_context.title: reduce goroutine leakage in `test/integration/controlplane/transformation`
issue_context.body:
Following up on https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/pull/111126#discussion_r935087747 to shutdown the gRPC goroutines and reduce the number of leaked goroutines.

/sig auth
comments: @aramase if you are too busy, just add a description on where the problem is and, if possible, suggestions on how to fix it, there is always people wanting to help with these things

Comment [#108483(comment)](https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/108483#issuecomment-1195714805) might help.

> The goroutines are coming from the fact that we're not closing the kms transformer (grpc goroutines) that is being created.
We basically create a grpc service and never close that:

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/18ce801beac34489f313d6b1223a1a5f07200cb6/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/options/encryptionconfig/config.go#L245

> Fixing would probably require changing transformer interfact to implement Close method or sth like that.

@aojea Thanks for your demo, And I would like to work on this.
/assign @sanwishe

review_comments: please add defer HandleCrash() - we generally try to do that in all goroutines (in production code) for safety

My small concern with this is that draining currently doesn't drain long-running requests, in particular watches.

However, watches can also require KMS or decrypting stuff they receive from etcd.

It's technically not end of the world, because it will just result in sending an error event:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/master/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/storage/etcd3/watcher.go#L331
and watchers should recover from it.
But in some cases, it may cause unnecessary relists:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/09e8339ae4e575ec40e8ed0fc2829fcb678c0f19/staging/src/k8s.io/client-go/tools/cache/reflector.go#L473
[FWIW - I wanted to address it for some time, but never got to it...]

I'm wondering if we shouldn't use some other signal, like HTTPServerStoppedListening in the meantime.

I'm not familiar with this, but it seems the apiserver stops to receive request a few steps earlier

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/253acfc8bce430ed835f14d5ec062356701cff2f/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/genericapiserver.go#L417-L458

has to be this the last thing stopping?

I'm confused... I thought we stopped listening for new connections prior to inflight requests being drained:

```
T0+70s: HTTPServerStoppedListening:
	- this event is signaled when the HTTP Server has stopped listening
      which is immediately after server.Shutdown has been invoked

T0 + 70s + up-to 60s: InFlightRequestsDrained: existing in flight requests have been drained
	- long running requests are outside of this scope
	- up-to 60s: the default value of 'ShutdownTimeout' is 60s, this means that
      any request in flight has a hard timeout of 60s.
	- it's time to call 'Shutdown' on the audit events since all
	  in flight request(s) have drained.
```

that would seem to indicate we should use InFlightRequestsDrained not HTTPServerStoppedListening, right?
put another way, it sounds like using HTTPServerStoppedListening means in-flight write requests will now fail, not just in-flight long-lived watch requests

I'm not sure I follow, listening vs accepting has different meanings 

https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/9644edc321e3b7e5180eb7c15a27bf28e19485db/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/genericapiserver.go#L563-L564

> that would seem to indicate we should use InFlightRequestsDrained not HTTPServerStoppedListening, right?

As I mentioned above, InFlightRequestsDrained does NOT include long-running requests. So that's not perfect.
@liggitt - I think the comment you pasted, is not really up-to-date.

I would appreciate if someone would double check me, but the  HTTPServerStoppedListening channel:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/253acfc8bce430ed835f14d5ec062356701cff2f/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/genericapiserver.go#L539

is effectively closed here:
https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/blob/253acfc8bce430ed835f14d5ec062356701cff2f/staging/src/k8s.io/apiserver/pkg/server/secure_serving.go#L242
So when http server is already down. Which basically happens after the requests are drained.


I agree that HTTPServerStoppedListening is not a perfect signal [we're probably missing one more signal], but I still think it's better than the Drained one which doesn't include long-running requests.

After reading the code I believe:

Neither `InFlightRequestsDrained` nor `HTTPServerStoppedListening` handle long running requests.  We have no option to handle that case AFAIK.

>  So when http server is already down. Which basically happens after the requests are drained.
> 
> I agree that HTTPServerStoppedListening is not a perfect signal [we're probably missing one more signal], but I still think it's better than the Drained one which doesn't include long-running requests.

This is not true.  `HTTPServerStoppedListening` corresponds to the listener socket being closed.  It does not close connections that have already been accepted (i.e. watches) by that socket (they have distinct FDs).

Thus I believe `InFlightRequestsDrained` is the best option available to us because:

1. We know new connections will not be made
2. We know that we have attempted to drain non-long running requests

> Thus I believe InFlightRequestsDrained is the best option available to us because:
>
> 1. We know new connections will not be made
> 2. We know that we have attempted to drain non-long running requests

that makes sense to me
please add defer HandleCrash() - we generally try to do that in all goroutines (in production code) for safety
